Theorem~\ref{thm:feas} the feasibility conclusions of all four anchors are unaffected.

\begin{theorem}[Structure of the certified law]\label{thm:struct}
For all $\mu, P$: (i) $S(\mu,P) = S(1-\mu,1-P)$; (ii) $S(\mu,P) = S(P,\mu)$; (iii)
$S(\mu,P) > 1$ strictly on the open box; (iv) for $0 < \mu < \tfrac12$ the map
$P \mapsto S(\mu,P)$ is strictly increasing.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) and (ii) are polynomial identities in $D$. (iii) is $D<1$, since
$1 - D = \mu(1-P) + P(1-\mu) > 0$. (iv) reduces after cross-multiplication to
$(Q-P)(1-2\mu) > 0$ for $P < Q$.
\end{proof}

Item (ii) is the formal content of the slogan ``balance is position'': the geometric
coordinate $\mu$ and the probabilistic coordinate $P$ enter the law identically.

\section{Composition: a coupling reading}

$D(\mu,P)$ is exactly the probability that two independent Bernoulli variables with
parameters $\mu$ and $P$ take the same value, so the certified value is the reciprocal of
an agreement probability. Stacking two independent stratifications multiplies the bookings:
the composite retained fraction is $\mu_1\mu_2$ and the composite capture probability is
$P_1P_2$.

\begin{theorem}[Coupling slack identity]\label{thm:coupling}
For all $a,b,c,d$,
\[
  D(ac, bd) - D(a,b)D(c,d)
   = (1-a)b(1-d) + a(1-b)(1-c) + (1-a)(1-b)\bigl((1-c)d + c(1-d)\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expand both sides. Probabilistically, the event ``the two products agree'' strictly
contains the event ``both coordinate pairs agree'', and the right-hand side enumerates the
extra configurations.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict submultiplicativity]\label{thm:submult}
On the open box $0 < a,b,c,d < 1$ we have $S(ac,bd) < S(a,b)S(c,d)$. The pathwise product
genuinely fails: at $(\tfrac12,\tfrac9{10})$ and $(\tfrac12,1)$ the composite value is
$S(\tfrac14,\tfrac9{10}) = \tfrac{10}{3}$ while the product of the factor values is $4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Every term on the right of Theorem~\ref{thm:coupling} is positive on the open box, so
$D(ac,bd) > D(a,b)D(c,d) > 0$; invert.
\end{proof}

Composed guarantees may therefore be reported as products of factor values: the product is
conservative, never optimistic.

\section{The canonical reporting prior}

If balance is position (Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}(ii)), the natural coordinate is the
\emph{balance coordinate} $s = r^{-1/2}$ for a scale variable $r \ge 1$.

\begin{definition}
The \emph{canonical kernel} is $b(r) = 1/(2r\sqrt r) = \tfrac12 r^{-3/2}$; the
\emph{capture CDF} is $x(r) = 1 - r^{-1/2}$. For a reporting density $g$ the
\emph{capture curve} is $P_g(R) = \bigl(\int_1^R g\bigr)/\bigl(\int_1^{R_{\max}} g\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform in the balance coordinate]\label{thm:canon}
For $R \ge 1$, $\int_1^R b(r)\,dr = 1 - R^{-1/2}$: the mass the canonical prior assigns to
$[1,R]$ is the length of the balance interval $[R^{-1/2}, 1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$x$ is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ with $x' = b$; apply the fundamental theorem of
calculus with $x(1) = 0$, $b$ being continuous on $[1,R]$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exactly linear capture]\label{thm:linear}
For $1 \le R$ and $1 < R_{\max}$, the canonical capture curve is
$P(R) = (1 - R^{-1/2})/(1 - R_{\max}^{-1/2})$; in the coordinate
$\mu = 1 - R^{-1/2}$ this reads $P(\mu) = \mu/(1 - R_{\max}^{-1/2})$, exactly linear.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear iff canonical]\label{thm:unique}
Let $g$ be continuous with $\int_1^R g = c\,x(R)$ for all $R \ge 1$ and some constant $c$.
Then $g(r) = c\,b(r)$ for every $r > 1$. The characterisation has content: the uniform
density on $[1,R_{\max}]$ fails it, giving capture $1/3$ at $R_{\max}=4$, $R=2$ where the
canonical curve gives $2 - \sqrt2 \approx 0.5858$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Differentiate the hypothesis in $R$; continuity of $g$ makes the derivative of the integral
equal to $g$, and $x' = b$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The four measured anchors, read through the canonical prior, demand extremely balanced
populations, with required scale ratio $R \approx 1.04$--$1.14$. Such populations are not
typical of the workloads the anchors were taken from, so the anchors are best interpreted
as generator-shape estimators rather than as witnesses of an achieved value.
\end{remark}

\section{Algorithms}

\paragraph{(A) Envelope evaluation.} Given bookings $(M,m,P)$, return
$[\,P + (1-P)(m+1),\ Pm + (1-P)M\,]$ and the booked point value \eqref{eq:booked}; cost
$O(1)$. By Theorems~\ref{thm:env}--\ref{thm:sharp} the interval is the exact range of $\EC$
over admissible weights, so a measured cost outside it certifies a booking violation.

\paragraph{(B) Certified-value audit.} Given $(\mu,\hat P)$, a slot count $M$ and a stated
baseline, return the full-scan value $1/D$, the descending-baseline value
$S(M+1)/(2M)$, the feasibility slack $(1-\hat P)(1-2\mu)$, and the rounding sensitivity
$|S(\mu,\hat P) - S(\mu, \mathrm{round}(\hat P))|$; cost $O(1)$. Running this audit on
$(0.02, 0.9853)$ surfaces the erratum.

\paragraph{(C) Adversarial locus search.} Since $D$ is bilinear with
$\partial_\mu D = 2P-1$ and $\partial_P D = 2\mu - 1$, its extrema over an axis-aligned
admissible box are attained at corners; the search is therefore $O(1)$ per box.
Theorem~\ref{thm:adv} is the output at the anchor $(0.05, 0.85)$.

\section{Discussion}

The framework separates into three tiers. \emph{Identities}: the $\rbar$-identity, the
$\Theta$-form law, the Chebyshev double-sum identity, the coupling slack identity, the
derivation of the block law. \emph{Unconditional inequalities}: the booked envelope,
majorization with its strict form, pigeonhole, the master inequality, submultiplicativity,
the feasibility test. \emph{Conditional closed forms}: the uniform-cells value law --- exact
on uniform cells, admissible as a report, unbounded in error as a guarantee, and both
baseline- and locus-dependent even when exact. Confusing the third tier for the second is
the error diagnosed here; the erratum is the same habit at the level of arithmetic hygiene.

Four reporting conventions follow: state the law with its bookings; use the canonical prior
$b \propto r^{-3/2}$; store raw unrounded measurements and report the descending-baseline
correction; and name the baseline of every value claim, since the ambiguity is a factor of
nearly two.

Limitations: the framework is one-shot and does not model adaptive re-stratification; the
composition theory treats independent stages only; cost kernels are deterministic functions
of the resolved slot; the canonical-prior characterisation assumes continuity. A converse
to the master inequality --- an algorithm attaining
$\min(1/(\Lambda\Theta\hat q), 2^k/(\Lambda\Theta))$ --- remains open.

\section{Future directions}

\paragraph{Envelope-optimal bookings.} The envelope is sharp given $(m,M,P)$ but has width
$P(m-1) + (1-P)(M-m-1)$. Booking one more statistic --- the within-cell second moment, or
$\Theta$ itself --- should collapse it quadratically, since $\Theta$ is exactly the
first-order shape statistic the envelope is blind to. The $\Theta$-form law is already
exact, so the missing step is a sharp bound on $\Theta$ in terms of an entropy or variance
budget.

\paragraph{Information-theoretic master constant.} The $2^k$ branch ignores the
distribution of bucket sizes. Replacing counting by entropy should give
$S \le 2^{H(\mathrm{bucket})}/(\Lambda\Theta)$ with $H \le k$, strictly better for
unbalanced filters: the worst-case bucket is a maximum while the expected probe count is an
average, and the gap is a R\'enyi-entropy deficit. The pigeonhole step is the only
combinatorial input to the chain, so it can be swapped in isolation.

\paragraph{Strict-majorization stability.} Conjecture: the defect obeys
$C_0 - C_{\mathrm{sort}} \ge c\,M\,\lVert w - u\rVert_1^2$, since the Chebyshev double sum
is a positive-definite quadratic form in $w$ once the cost kernel is strictly increasing,
making the defect a squared distance in disguise. The double-sum identity is the hard half
of any quantitative version.

\paragraph{Composition semigroup of loci.} $D$ is a Bernoulli agreement probability and the
coupling slack identity quantifies the failure of multiplicativity exactly. Do the loci form
a semigroup under a renormalised composition that \emph{is} multiplicative, and what are its
fixed points?

\section{Conclusion}

A closed-form speedup law is a compression of an identity. The identity here,
$\EC = P\rbar_R + (1-P)\rbar_C$, is exact and universal; the compression is not. We have
shown what the compression assumes, by how much it can fail, what replaces it, and what it
silently fixes when it is exact --- a baseline worth a factor of nearly two and a locus
worth a few percent. We have corrected a printed anchor computed at a rounded input and
proved that the feasibility conclusions drawn from that table survive the correction. Book
your averages, name your baseline, keep your raw digits.

\end{document}

"""
Positional-stratum measure framework: numerical demonstrations.

Self-contained (standard library only). Every function is inlined and type-hinted.

The script demonstrates, numerically:

  1. The r-bar identity        EC = P * rbar_R + (1 - P) * rbar_C   (exact, universal).
  2. The booking factor Theta  = rbar_R / centre(R): Theta = 1 on uniform cells,
     Theta = 1 does NOT imply uniformity on a single cell.
  3. Unbounded failure of the booked (uniform-cells) value law.
  4. The sharp booked envelope, attained at both ends.
  5. Majorization: a descending weight beats the baseline C0 = (M+1)/2, strictly
     unless flat.
  6. Pigeonhole on a k-bit filter and the master inequality.
  7. The certified block law S(mu, P) = 1 / (mu*P + (1-mu)(1-P)); baseline
     conditionality; an adversarial locus undercut.
  8. The feasibility test mu <= 1/S and the anchor-table erratum
     (0.02, 0.9853) -> 29.3152..., not 29.0698... .
  9. Composition: 1/S is a Bernoulli agreement probability; strict
     submultiplicativity.
 10. The canonical reporting prior b(r) = 0.5 * r^{-3/2} and its exactly linear
     capture curve.

Run:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple
import math
import random

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core framework
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def expected_cost(cost: Sequence[float], weight: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """EC = sum_i c(i) w(i) over the positional space {1, ..., M}."""
    return sum(c * w for c, w in zip(cost, weight))


def mass(weight: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Total weight carried by a stratum, given as 0-based indices."""
    return sum(weight[i] for i in stratum)


def rbar(cost: Sequence[float], weight: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Conditional mean cost inside a stratum: rbar_R = sum_R c w / mass_R."""
    m = mass(weight, stratum)
    if m == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("degenerate stratum: zero mass")
    return sum(cost[i] * weight[i] for i in stratum) / m


def cell_centre(cost: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Unweighted mean of the cost kernel on a stratum."""
    return sum(cost[i] for i in stratum) / len(stratum)


def theta(cost: Sequence[float], weight: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Booking factor Theta_R = rbar_R / centre(R)."""
    return rbar(cost, weight, stratum) / cell_centre(cost, stratum)


def scan_kernel(M: int) -> List[float]:
    """Scan cost kernel c(i) = i on slots 1..M (returned 0-based)."""
    return [float(i + 1) for i in range(M)]


def booked_ec(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> float:
    """Uniform-within-cells booked expected scan cost for a head stratum of size m."""
    return P * ((m + 1) / 2.0) + (1.0 - P) * (m + (M - m + 1) / 2.0)


def envelope(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Sharp two-sided booked envelope for EC given only the bookings (M, m, P)."""
    lower = P * 1.0 + (1.0 - P) * (m + 1)
    upper = P * m + (1.0 - P) * M
    return lower, upper


def head_witness(m: int) -> List[float]:
    """Lower-envelope witness on M = 2m slots: mass 1-1/m at slot 1, 1/m at slot m+1."""
    M = 2 * m
    w = [0.0] * M
    w[0] = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
    w[m] = 1.0 / m
    return w


def tail_witness(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> List[float]:
    """Upper-envelope witness: mass P at slot m, mass 1-P at slot M."""
    w = [0.0] * M
    w[m - 1] += P
    w[M - 1] += 1.0 - P
    return w


def baseline_c0(M: int) -> float:
    """Descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2."""
    return (M + 1) / 2.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The certified block law
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def agreement(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """D(mu, P) = mu P + (1-mu)(1-P): the Bernoulli agreement probability = 1/S."""
    return mu * P + (1.0 - mu) * (1.0 - P)


def certified_value(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """S(mu, P) = 1 / D(mu, P), the value against the full-scan-M baseline."""
    return 1.0 / agreement(mu, P)


def block_ec(M: float, mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """Simultaneous-commitment expected cost: M * D(mu, P)."""
    return M * agreement(mu, P)


def desc_value(M: float, mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """Value of the same algorithm against the descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2."""
    return ((M + 1.0) / 2.0) / block_ec(M, mu, P)


def feasibility_slack(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """D(mu,P) - mu = (1-P)(1-2mu): nonnegative on the admissible half-box mu <= 1/2."""
    return agreement(mu, P) - mu


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Canonical reporting prior
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def canonical_kernel(r: float) -> float:
    """b(r) = 1 / (2 r sqrt r) = 0.5 * r^{-3/2}."""
    return 1.0 / (2.0 * r * math.sqrt(r))


def capture_cdf(R: float) -> float:
    """x(R) = 1 - R^{-1/2}: the primitive of the canonical kernel, x(1) = 0."""
    return 1.0 - 1.0 / math.sqrt(R)


def capture_prob(Rmax: float, R: float) -> float:
    """Capture curve of the canonical prior, normalised on [1, Rmax]."""
    return capture_cdf(R) / capture_cdf(Rmax)


def numeric_integral(f: Callable[[float], float], a: float, b: float, n: int = 200000) -> float:
    """Composite Simpson rule (n even)."""
    if n % 2:
        n += 1
    h = (b - a) / n
    total = f(a) + f(b)
    for i in range(1, n):
        total += (4.0 if i % 2 else 2.0) * f(a + i * h)
    return total * h / 3.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_rbar_identity() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("1. The r-bar identity  EC = P*rbar_R + (1-P)*rbar_C   (exact, universal)")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(20260825)
    worst = 0.0
    for trial in range(8):
        M = rng.randint(4, 40)
        raw = [rng.random() ** rng.choice([0.3, 1.0, 3.0]) for _ in range(M)]
        tot = sum(raw)
        w = [x / tot for x in raw]
        # an arbitrary (even non-monotone) cost kernel
        c = [rng.uniform(0.5, 10.0) * (i + 1) ** rng.choice([0.5, 1.0]) for i in range(M)]
        k = rng.randint(1, M - 1)
        R = list(range(k))
        C = list(range(k, M))
        P = mass(w, R)
        lhs = expected_cost(c, w)
        rhs = P * rbar(c, w, R) + (1.0 - P) * rbar(c, w, C)
        err = abs(lhs - rhs) / abs(lhs)
        worst = max(worst, err)
        print(f"  M={M:3d}  |R|={k:3d}  P={P:.4f}   EC={lhs:10.5f}   "
              f"P*rbar_R+(1-P)*rbar_C={rhs:10.5f}   rel.err={err:.2e}")
    print(f"  -> worst relative error over 8 random cells: {worst:.3e} (identity, exact)")
    print()


def demo_theta() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("2. The booking factor Theta = rbar_R / centre(R)")
    print("=" * 78)
    M = 8
    c = scan_kernel(M)
    uniform = [1.0 / M] * M
    R = list(range(M))
    print(f"  uniform weight on 8 slots:  Theta = {theta(c, uniform, R):.12f}  (= 1 exactly)")

    # Single-cell converse fails: (1/2, 0, 1/2) on three slots has Theta = 1.
    c3 = scan_kernel(3)
    w3 = [0.5, 0.0, 0.5]
    print(f"  weight (1/2, 0, 1/2) on 3 slots: rbar = {rbar(c3, w3, [0, 1, 2]):.6f}, "
          f"centre = {cell_centre(c3, [0, 1, 2]):.6f}, Theta = {theta(c3, w3, [0,1,2]):.12f}")
    print("  -> Theta = 1 on ONE cell does not certify uniformity (w1 = 1/2 != 0 = w2).")

    # Theta == 1 on all pairs does force uniformity: check the pair criterion.
    print("  pair test on the non-uniform weight above, R = {1,2}: "
          f"Theta = {theta(c3, [0.5, 0.0, 0.5], [0, 1]):.6f} != 1  "
          "(so the all-cells criterion correctly rejects it)")
    print()


def demo_value_universality_fails() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3. Value-universality fails, unboundedly (head witness on M = 2m)")
    print("=" * 78)
    print("     m      P = 1-1/m     true EC   booked EC   booked/true")
    for m in (4, 8, 32, 128, 1024, 8192):
        M = 2 * m
        w = head_witness(m)
        c = scan_kernel(M)
        P = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
        true_ec = expected_cost(c, w)
        bk = booked_ec(M, m, P)
        print(f"  {m:6d}   {P:.8f}   {true_ec:9.5f}   {bk:9.2f}   {bk/true_ec:11.2f}")
    print("  -> true EC is exactly 2 for every m; the booked prediction is (m+3)/2.")
    print("     The ratio is unbounded, so the booked value law is not an upper bound.")
    print()


def demo_envelope() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4. The sharp booked envelope, attained at both ends")
    print("=" * 78)
    m, M = 16, 32
    P = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
    lo, hi = envelope(M, m, P)
    c = scan_kernel(M)
    ec_head = expected_cost(c, head_witness(m))
    ec_tail = expected_cost(c, tail_witness(M, m, P))
    bk = booked_ec(M, m, P)
    print(f"  bookings (M, m, P) = ({M}, {m}, {P:.6f})")
    print(f"  envelope      : [{lo:.6f}, {hi:.6f}]   (width {hi-lo:.6f})")
    print(f"  head witness  : EC = {ec_head:.6f}   (lower end, gap {abs(ec_head-lo):.2e})")
    print(f"  tail witness  : EC = {ec_tail:.6f}   (upper end, gap {abs(ec_tail-hi):.2e})")
    print(f"  booked value  : EC = {bk:.6f}   inside envelope: {lo <= bk <= hi}")

    # random admissible weights all land inside
    rng = random.Random(7)
    inside = 0
    trials = 2000
    for _ in range(trials):
        head = [rng.random() for _ in range(m)]
        tail = [rng.random() for _ in range(M - m)]
        hs, ts = sum(head), sum(tail)
        w = [P * x / hs for x in head] + [(1 - P) * x / ts for x in tail]
        ec = expected_cost(c, w)
        inside += (lo - 1e-9 <= ec <= hi + 1e-9)
    print(f"  {inside}/{trials} random admissible weights inside the envelope "
          f"({100.0*inside/trials:.1f}%)")
    print()


def demo_majorization() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("5. Majorization: a descending weight beats C0 = (M+1)/2, strictly unless flat")
    print("=" * 78)
    M = 32
    c = scan_kernel(M)
    C0 = baseline_c0(M)
    flat = [1.0 / M] * M
    print(f"  flat weight        : EC = {expected_cost(c, flat):.6f}   C0 = {C0:.6f}  "
          f"(equality)")
    rng = random.Random(11)
    worst_defect = 0.0
    for label, gen in (
        ("geometric  p=0.9", lambda i: 0.9 ** i),
        ("power law  1/i^2", lambda i: 1.0 / (i + 1) ** 2),
        ("linear ramp     ", lambda i: float(M - i)),
    ):
        raw = [gen(i) for i in range(M)]
        s = sum(raw)
        w = [x / s for x in raw]
        ec = expected_cost(c, w)
        worst_defect = max(worst_defect, C0 - ec)
        print(f"  {label}: EC = {ec:9.6f}   defect C0 - EC = {C0 - ec:9.6f}  (> 0)")
    # rearrangement: sorting descending is optimal
    raw = [rng.random() for _ in range(M)]
    s = sum(raw)
    w_sorted = sorted((x / s for x in raw), reverse=True)
    best = expected_cost(c, w_sorted)
    worse = min(expected_cost(c, random.Random(k).sample(w_sorted, M)) for k in range(200))
    print(f"  rearrangement: sorted EC = {best:.6f} <= best of 200 shuffles = {worse:.6f}")
    print()


def demo_master_inequality() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6. Pigeonhole on a k-bit filter and the master inequality")
    print("=" * 78)
    M, k = 4096, 5
    rng = random.Random(3)
    buckets: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for i in range(M):
        b = rng.randrange(2 ** k)
        buckets[b] = buckets.get(b, 0) + 1
    largest = max(buckets.values())
    print(f"  M = {M} slots into 2^{k} = {2**k} buckets: largest bucket = {largest} "
          f">= M/2^k = {M / 2**k:.1f}   (pigeonhole holds: {largest >= M / 2**k})")
    lam, th, qhat = 1.2, 0.95, 0.30
    Cdesc = 1000.0
    branch_q = 1.0 / (lam * th * qhat)
    branch_k = (2.0 ** k) / (lam * th)
    cap = min(branch_q, branch_k)
    CA = max(lam * th * qhat * Cdesc, M / 2 ** k)
    S = Cdesc / CA
    print(f"  bookings Lambda={lam}, Theta={th}, qhat={qhat}, k={k}")
    print(f"  branch 1: 1/(L*T*q)   = {branch_q:.6f}")
    print(f"  branch 2: 2^k/(L*T)   = {branch_k:.6f}")
    print(f"  master cap = min      = {cap:.6f};  realised S = {S:.6f};  "
          f"S <= cap: {S <= cap + 1e-12}")
    print()


def demo_certified_law_and_baseline() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("7. The certified block law, and its baseline conditionality")
    print("=" * 78)
    mu, P = 0.05, 0.85
    print(f"  anchor (mu, P) = ({mu}, {P}):  D = {agreement(mu, P):.6f}, "
          f"S = {certified_value(mu, P):.10f}  (= 200/37)")
    print("      M      S_full-scan     S_descending     ratio (M+1)/(2M)")
    for M in (10, 100, 1000, 10 ** 6):
        S = certified_value(mu, P)
        Sd = desc_value(float(M), mu, P)
        print(f"  {M:8d}   {S:12.6f}   {Sd:14.6f}   {(M+1)/(2*M):16.8f}")
    print("  -> S/2 < S_descending < S always; the certified number asymptotically")
    print("     DOUBLES the value the same algorithm has against C0 = (M+1)/2.")

    print()
    print("  Adversarial locus (same prior, mu nudged from 0.050 to 0.052):")
    print(f"    S(0.050, 0.85) = {certified_value(0.05, 0.85):.6f}")
    print(f"    S(0.052, 0.85) = {certified_value(0.052, 0.85):.6f}   "
          f"undercut: {certified_value(0.052, 0.85) < certified_value(0.05, 0.85)}")
    print()


def demo_feasibility_and_erratum() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("8. Feasibility test and the anchor-table erratum")
    print("=" * 78)
    stored = Fraction(9853, 10000)
    rounded = Fraction(985, 1000)
    mu = Fraction(2, 100)

    def exact_S(m: Fraction, p: Fraction) -> Fraction:
        return 1 / (m * p + (1 - m) * (1 - p))

    S_stored = exact_S(mu, stored)
    S_rounded = exact_S(mu, rounded)
    print(f"  stored  P-hat = 0.9853 :  S = {S_stored} = {float(S_stored):.6f}")
    print(f"  rounded P     = 0.985  :  S = {S_rounded} = {float(S_rounded):.6f}")
    print("  the printed table entry 29.0698... is the ROUNDED value; the correct")
    print(f"  entry at the stored measurement is {float(S_stored):.4f}   "
          f"(shift {float(S_stored - S_rounded):.4f})")
    print()
    print("  Feasibility  mu <= 1/S  on the admissible half-box (slack = (1-P)(1-2mu)):")
    for m_, p_ in ((0.02, 0.9853), (0.02, 0.985), (0.05, 0.85), (0.115, 0.87),
                   (0.30, 0.60), (0.50, 0.99)):
        slack = feasibility_slack(m_, p_)
        print(f"    mu={m_:5.3f}  P={p_:6.4f}  S={certified_value(m_, p_):8.4f}  "
              f"1/S={1/certified_value(m_, p_):.6f}  slack={slack:+.6f}  "
              f"feasible={slack >= -1e-15}")
    print("  -> the verdict never flips: it is insensitive to the precision of P-hat.")
    print()
    print("  Superseded / stale readings:")
    for label, val in (("drafted 5.19 window", 5.1948), ("certified anchor", 5.4054)):
        print(f"    {label:22s}: {val}")
    print(f"    stale locus (0.115, 0.87): S = {certified_value(0.115, 0.87):.4f}")
    print()


def demo_composition() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("9. Composition: 1/S is a Bernoulli agreement probability")
    print("=" * 78)
    # Monte-Carlo check that D is an agreement probability.
    rng = random.Random(99)
    mu, P = 0.37, 0.71
    n = 400000
    agree = sum(1 for _ in range(n) if (rng.random() < mu) == (rng.random() < P))
    print(f"  D({mu}, {P}) = {agreement(mu, P):.6f}   Monte-Carlo agreement rate = "
          f"{agree/n:.6f}   (n = {n})")
    print()
    print("  Strict submultiplicativity  S(mu1*mu2, P1*P2) < S1 * S2:")
    print("      (mu1,P1)      (mu2,P2)     composite      product      slack")
    for (a, b, c_, d) in ((0.5, 0.9, 0.5, 0.999), (0.2, 0.8, 0.4, 0.7),
                          (0.05, 0.85, 0.1, 0.9), (0.3, 0.6, 0.3, 0.6)):
        comp = certified_value(a * c_, b * d)
        prod = certified_value(a, b) * certified_value(c_, d)
        print(f"   ({a:.2f},{b:.3f})  ({c_:.2f},{d:.3f})  {comp:10.6f}  {prod:10.6f}  "
              f"{prod - comp:+.6f}")
    print("  boundary case (mu1,P1)=(1/2,9/10), (mu2,P2)=(1/2,1): "
          f"composite = {certified_value(0.25, 0.9):.6f}, product = "
          f"{certified_value(0.5, 0.9) * certified_value(0.5, 1.0):.6f}")
    print("  -> reporting a composed guarantee as a product is conservative, never")
    print("     optimistic.")
    print()


def demo_canonical_prior() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("10. The canonical reporting prior b(r) = 0.5 r^{-3/2}")
    print("=" * 78)
    for R in (1.5, 2.0, 4.0, 10.0, 100.0):
        num = numeric_integral(canonical_kernel, 1.0, R, 20000)
        print(f"  R = {R:7.2f}:  integral_1^R b = {num:.8f}   1 - R^(-1/2) = "
              f"{capture_cdf(R):.8f}   (balance-interval length)")
    print()
    Rmax = 25.0
    print(f"  Capture curve is exactly linear in mu = 1 - R^(-1/2)  (Rmax = {Rmax}):")
    print("       R        mu        P(R)      mu/(1-Rmax^(-1/2))")
    slope_den = 1.0 - 1.0 / math.sqrt(Rmax)
    for R in (1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 12.0, 25.0):
        mu_ = capture_cdf(R)
        print(f"  {R:7.2f}  {mu_:8.6f}  {capture_prob(Rmax, R):8.6f}  "
              f"{mu_/slope_den:18.6f}")
    print()
    print("  A non-canonical (uniform) prior fails the linearity test:")
    unif = (2.0 - 1.0) / (4.0 - 1.0)
    print(f"    uniform on [1,4], capture at R=2 : {unif:.6f}")
    print(f"    canonical         capture at R=2 : {capture_prob(4.0, 2.0):.6f}  "
          f"(= 2 - sqrt 2)")
    print("  -> linear capture curve IFF canonical kernel.")
    print()


def main() -> None:
    print()
    print("POSITIONAL-STRATUM MEASURE FRAMEWORK -- NUMERICAL DEMONSTRATIONS")
    print()
    demo_rbar_identity()
    demo_theta()
    demo_value_universality_fails()
    demo_envelope()
    demo_majorization()
    demo_master_inequality()
    demo_certified_law_and_baseline()
    demo_feasibility_and_erratum()
    demo_composition()
    demo_canonical_prior()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("Summary: the r-bar identity is exact and universal; the booked value law")
    print("is a reporting convention whose failure is unbounded; the envelope and the")
    print("master inequality are the guarded statements that survive; and every value")
    print("claim is conditional on a named baseline and a pinned locus.")
    print("=" * 78)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

demos.description: A ten-part self-contained numerical tour of the whole framework. It verifies the r̄-identity to machine precision on random weights, random cost kernels and random strata; exhibits Θ = 1 on a non-uniform cell; tabulates the unbounded divergence between the uniform-cells booked prediction and the true cost of the head witness; confirms the sharp envelope numerically, including attainment at both ends and containment of two thousand random admissible weights; measures the majorization defect C₀ − EC for several descending priors and checks that sorting beats every shuffle; demonstrates pigeonhole on a 5-bit filter and the resulting master cap; tabulates the baseline bracket S/2 < S_desc < S as M grows; reproduces the anchor-table erratum in exact rational arithmetic together with the feasibility slack; validates by Monte Carlo that 1/S is a Bernoulli agreement probability and that composition is strictly submultiplicative; and integrates the canonical kernel numerically to confirm its exactly linear capture curve.
demos.code:
"""
Positional-stratum measure framework: numerical demonstrations.

Self-contained (standard library only). Every function is inlined and type-hinted.

The script demonstrates, numerically:

  1. The r-bar identity        EC = P * rbar_R + (1 - P) * rbar_C   (exact, universal).
  2. The booking factor Theta  = rbar_R / centre(R): Theta = 1 on uniform cells,
     Theta = 1 does NOT imply uniformity on a single cell.
  3. Unbounded failure of the booked (uniform-cells) value law.
  4. The sharp booked envelope, attained at both ends.
  5. Majorization: a descending weight beats the baseline C0 = (M+1)/2, strictly
     unless flat.
  6. Pigeonhole on a k-bit filter and the master inequality.
  7. The certified block law S(mu, P) = 1 / (mu*P + (1-mu)(1-P)); baseline
     conditionality; an adversarial locus undercut.
  8. The feasibility test mu <= 1/S and the anchor-table erratum
     (0.02, 0.9853) -> 29.3152..., not 29.0698... .
  9. Composition: 1/S is a Bernoulli agreement probability; strict
     submultiplicativity.
 10. The canonical reporting prior b(r) = 0.5 * r^{-3/2} and its exactly linear
     capture curve.

Run:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple
import math
import random

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core framework
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def expected_cost(cost: Sequence[float], weight: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """EC = sum_i c(i) w(i) over the positional space {1, ..., M}."""
    return sum(c * w for c, w in zip(cost, weight))


def mass(weight: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Total weight carried by a stratum, given as 0-based indices."""
    return sum(weight[i] for i in stratum)


def rbar(cost: Sequence[float], weight: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Conditional mean cost inside a stratum: rbar_R = sum_R c w / mass_R."""
    m = mass(weight, stratum)
    if m == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("degenerate stratum: zero mass")
    return sum(cost[i] * weight[i] for i in stratum) / m


def cell_centre(cost: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Unweighted mean of the cost kernel on a stratum."""
    return sum(cost[i] for i in stratum) / len(stratum)


def theta(cost: Sequence[float], weight: Sequence[float], stratum: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Booking factor Theta_R = rbar_R / centre(R)."""
    return rbar(cost, weight, stratum) / cell_centre(cost, stratum)


def scan_kernel(M: int) -> List[float]:
    """Scan cost kernel c(i) = i on slots 1..M (returned 0-based)."""
    return [float(i + 1) for i in range(M)]


def booked_ec(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> float:
    """Uniform-within-cells booked expected scan cost for a head stratum of size m."""
    return P * ((m + 1) / 2.0) + (1.0 - P) * (m + (M - m + 1) / 2.0)


def envelope(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Sharp two-sided booked envelope for EC given only the bookings (M, m, P)."""
    lower = P * 1.0 + (1.0 - P) * (m + 1)
    upper = P * m + (1.0 - P) * M
    return lower, upper


def head_witness(m: int) -> List[float]:
    """Lower-envelope witness on M = 2m slots: mass 1-1/m at slot 1, 1/m at slot m+1."""
    M = 2 * m
    w = [0.0] * M
    w[0] = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
    w[m] = 1.0 / m
    return w


def tail_witness(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> List[float]:
    """Upper-envelope witness: mass P at slot m, mass 1-P at slot M."""
    w = [0.0] * M
    w[m - 1] += P
    w[M - 1] += 1.0 - P
    return w


def baseline_c0(M: int) -> float:
    """Descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2."""
    return (M + 1) / 2.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The certified block law
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def agreement(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """D(mu, P) = mu P + (1-mu)(1-P): the Bernoulli agreement probability = 1/S."""
    return mu * P + (1.0 - mu) * (1.0 - P)


def certified_value(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """S(mu, P) = 1 / D(mu, P), the value against the full-scan-M baseline."""
    return 1.0 / agreement(mu, P)


def block_ec(M: float, mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """Simultaneous-commitment expected cost: M * D(mu, P)."""
    return M * agreement(mu, P)


def desc_value(M: float, mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """Value of the same algorithm against the descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2."""
    return ((M + 1.0) / 2.0) / block_ec(M, mu, P)


def feasibility_slack(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """D(mu,P) - mu = (1-P)(1-2mu): nonnegative on the admissible half-box mu <= 1/2."""
    return agreement(mu, P) - mu


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Canonical reporting prior
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def canonical_kernel(r: float) -> float:
    """b(r) = 1 / (2 r sqrt r) = 0.5 * r^{-3/2}."""
    return 1.0 / (2.0 * r * math.sqrt(r))


def capture_cdf(R: float) -> float:
    """x(R) = 1 - R^{-1/2}: the primitive of the canonical kernel, x(1) = 0."""
    return 1.0 - 1.0 / math.sqrt(R)


def capture_prob(Rmax: float, R: float) -> float:
    """Capture curve of the canonical prior, normalised on [1, Rmax]."""
    return capture_cdf(R) / capture_cdf(Rmax)


def numeric_integral(f: Callable[[float], float], a: float, b: float, n: int = 200000) -> float:
    """Composite Simpson rule (n even)."""
    if n % 2:
        n += 1
    h = (b - a) / n
    total = f(a) + f(b)
    for i in range(1, n):
        total += (4.0 if i % 2 else 2.0) * f(a + i * h)
    return total * h / 3.0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_rbar_identity() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("1. The r-bar identity  EC = P*rbar_R + (1-P)*rbar_C   (exact, universal)")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(20260825)
    worst = 0.0
    for trial in range(8):
        M = rng.randint(4, 40)
        raw = [rng.random() ** rng.choice([0.3, 1.0, 3.0]) for _ in range(M)]
        tot = sum(raw)
        w = [x / tot for x in raw]
        # an arbitrary (even non-monotone) cost kernel
        c = [rng.uniform(0.5, 10.0) * (i + 1) ** rng.choice([0.5, 1.0]) for i in range(M)]
        k = rng.randint(1, M - 1)
        R = list(range(k))
        C = list(range(k, M))
        P = mass(w, R)
        lhs = expected_cost(c, w)
        rhs = P * rbar(c, w, R) + (1.0 - P) * rbar(c, w, C)
        err = abs(lhs - rhs) / abs(lhs)
        worst = max(worst, err)
        print(f"  M={M:3d}  |R|={k:3d}  P={P:.4f}   EC={lhs:10.5f}   "
              f"P*rbar_R+(1-P)*rbar_C={rhs:10.5f}   rel.err={err:.2e}")
    print(f"  -> worst relative error over 8 random cells: {worst:.3e} (identity, exact)")
    print()


def demo_theta() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("2. The booking factor Theta = rbar_R / centre(R)")
    print("=" * 78)
    M = 8
    c = scan_kernel(M)
    uniform = [1.0 / M] * M
    R = list(range(M))
    print(f"  uniform weight on 8 slots:  Theta = {theta(c, uniform, R):.12f}  (= 1 exactly)")

    # Single-cell converse fails: (1/2, 0, 1/2) on three slots has Theta = 1.
    c3 = scan_kernel(3)
    w3 = [0.5, 0.0, 0.5]
    print(f"  weight (1/2, 0, 1/2) on 3 slots: rbar = {rbar(c3, w3, [0, 1, 2]):.6f}, "
          f"centre = {cell_centre(c3, [0, 1, 2]):.6f}, Theta = {theta(c3, w3, [0,1,2]):.12f}")
    print("  -> Theta = 1 on ONE cell does not certify uniformity (w1 = 1/2 != 0 = w2).")

    # Theta == 1 on all pairs does force uniformity: check the pair criterion.
    print("  pair test on the non-uniform weight above, R = {1,2}: "
          f"Theta = {theta(c3, [0.5, 0.0, 0.5], [0, 1]):.6f} != 1  "
          "(so the all-cells criterion correctly rejects it)")
    print()


def demo_value_universality_fails() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3. Value-universality fails, unboundedly (head witness on M = 2m)")
    print("=" * 78)
    print("     m      P = 1-1/m     true EC   booked EC   booked/true")
    for m in (4, 8, 32, 128, 1024, 8192):
        M = 2 * m
        w = head_witness(m)
        c = scan_kernel(M)
        P = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
        true_ec = expected_cost(c, w)
        bk = booked_ec(M, m, P)
        print(f"  {m:6d}   {P:.8f}   {true_ec:9.5f}   {bk:9.2f}   {bk/true_ec:11.2f}")
    print("  -> true EC is exactly 2 for every m; the booked prediction is (m+3)/2.")
    print("     The ratio is unbounded, so the booked value law is not an upper bound.")
    print()


def demo_envelope() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4. The sharp booked envelope, attained at both ends")
    print("=" * 78)
    m, M = 16, 32
    P = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
    lo, hi = envelope(M, m, P)
    c = scan_kernel(M)
    ec_head = expected_cost(c, head_witness(m))
    ec_tail = expected_cost(c, tail_witness(M, m, P))
    bk = booked_ec(M, m, P)
    print(f"  bookings (M, m, P) = ({M}, {m}, {P:.6f})")
    print(f"  envelope      : [{lo:.6f}, {hi:.6f}]   (width {hi-lo:.6f})")
    print(f"  head witness  : EC = {ec_head:.6f}   (lower end, gap {abs(ec_head-lo):.2e})")
    print(f"  tail witness  : EC = {ec_tail:.6f}   (upper end, gap {abs(ec_tail-hi):.2e})")
    print(f"  booked value  : EC = {bk:.6f}   inside envelope: {lo <= bk <= hi}")

    # random admissible weights all land inside
    rng = random.Random(7)
    inside = 0
    trials = 2000
    for _ in range(trials):
        head = [rng.random() for _ in range(m)]
        tail = [rng.random() for _ in range(M - m)]
        hs, ts = sum(head), sum(tail)
        w = [P * x / hs for x in head] + [(1 - P) * x / ts for x in tail]
        ec = expected_cost(c, w)
        inside += (lo - 1e-9 <= ec <= hi + 1e-9)
    print(f"  {inside}/{trials} random admissible weights inside the envelope "
          f"({100.0*inside/trials:.1f}%)")
    print()


def demo_majorization() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("5. Majorization: a descending weight beats C0 = (M+1)/2, strictly unless flat")
    print("=" * 78)
    M = 32
    c = scan_kernel(M)
    C0 = baseline_c0(M)
    flat = [1.0 / M] * M
    print(f"  flat weight        : EC = {expected_cost(c, flat):.6f}   C0 = {C0:.6f}  "
          f"(equality)")
    rng = random.Random(11)
    worst_defect = 0.0
    for label, gen in (
        ("geometric  p=0.9", lambda i: 0.9 ** i),
        ("power law  1/i^2", lambda i: 1.0 / (i + 1) ** 2),
        ("linear ramp     ", lambda i: float(M - i)),
    ):
        raw = [gen(i) for i in range(M)]
        s = sum(raw)
        w = [x / s for x in raw]
        ec = expected_cost(c, w)
        worst_defect = max(worst_defect, C0 - ec)
        print(f"  {label}: EC = {ec:9.6f}   defect C0 - EC = {C0 - ec:9.6f}  (> 0)")
    # rearrangement: sorting descending is optimal
    raw = [rng.random() for _ in range(M)]
    s = sum(raw)
    w_sorted = sorted((x / s for x in raw), reverse=True)
    best = expected_cost(c, w_sorted)
    worse = min(expected_cost(c, random.Random(k).sample(w_sorted, M)) for k in range(200))
    print(f"  rearrangement: sorted EC = {best:.6f} <= best of 200 shuffles = {worse:.6f}")
    print()


def demo_master_inequality() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6. Pigeonhole on a k-bit filter and the master inequality")
    print("=" * 78)
    M, k = 4096, 5
    rng = random.Random(3)
    buckets: Dict[int, int] = {}
    for i in range(M):
        b = rng.randrange(2 ** k)
        buckets[b] = buckets.get(b, 0) + 1
    largest = max(buckets.values())
    print(f"  M = {M} slots into 2^{k} = {2**k} buckets: largest bucket = {largest} "
          f">= M/2^k = {M / 2**k:.1f}   (pigeonhole holds: {largest >= M / 2**k})")
    lam, th, qhat = 1.2, 0.95, 0.30
    Cdesc = 1000.0
    branch_q = 1.0 / (lam * th * qhat)
    branch_k = (2.0 ** k) / (lam * th)
    cap = min(branch_q, branch_k)
    CA = max(lam * th * qhat * Cdesc, M / 2 ** k)
    S = Cdesc / CA
    print(f"  bookings Lambda={lam}, Theta={th}, qhat={qhat}, k={k}")
    print(f"  branch 1: 1/(L*T*q)   = {branch_q:.6f}")
    print(f"  branch 2: 2^k/(L*T)   = {branch_k:.6f}")
    print(f"  master cap = min      = {cap:.6f};  realised S = {S:.6f};  "
          f"S <= cap: {S <= cap + 1e-12}")
    print()


def demo_certified_law_and_baseline() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("7. The certified block law, and its baseline conditionality")
    print("=" * 78)
    mu, P = 0.05, 0.85
    print(f"  anchor (mu, P) = ({mu}, {P}):  D = {agreement(mu, P):.6f}, "
          f"S = {certified_value(mu, P):.10f}  (= 200/37)")
    print("      M      S_full-scan     S_descending     ratio (M+1)/(2M)")
    for M in (10, 100, 1000, 10 ** 6):
        S = certified_value(mu, P)
        Sd = desc_value(float(M), mu, P)
        print(f"  {M:8d}   {S:12.6f}   {Sd:14.6f}   {(M+1)/(2*M):16.8f}")
    print("  -> S/2 < S_descending < S always; the certified number asymptotically")
    print("     DOUBLES the value the same algorithm has against C0 = (M+1)/2.")

    print()
    print("  Adversarial locus (same prior, mu nudged from 0.050 to 0.052):")
    print(f"    S(0.050, 0.85) = {certified_value(0.05, 0.85):.6f}")
    print(f"    S(0.052, 0.85) = {certified_value(0.052, 0.85):.6f}   "
          f"undercut: {certified_value(0.052, 0.85) < certified_value(0.05, 0.85)}")
    print()


def demo_feasibility_and_erratum() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("8. Feasibility test and the anchor-table erratum")
    print("=" * 78)
    stored = Fraction(9853, 10000)
    rounded = Fraction(985, 1000)
    mu = Fraction(2, 100)

    def exact_S(m: Fraction, p: Fraction) -> Fraction:
        return 1 / (m * p + (1 - m) * (1 - p))

    S_stored = exact_S(mu, stored)
    S_rounded = exact_S(mu, rounded)
    print(f"  stored  P-hat = 0.9853 :  S = {S_stored} = {float(S_stored):.6f}")
    print(f"  rounded P     = 0.985  :  S = {S_rounded} = {float(S_rounded):.6f}")
    print("  the printed table entry 29.0698... is the ROUNDED value; the correct")
    print(f"  entry at the stored measurement is {float(S_stored):.4f}   "
          f"(shift {float(S_stored - S_rounded):.4f})")
    print()
    print("  Feasibility  mu <= 1/S  on the admissible half-box (slack = (1-P)(1-2mu)):")
    for m_, p_ in ((0.02, 0.9853), (0.02, 0.985), (0.05, 0.85), (0.115, 0.87),
                   (0.30, 0.60), (0.50, 0.99)):
        slack = feasibility_slack(m_, p_)
        print(f"    mu={m_:5.3f}  P={p_:6.4f}  S={certified_value(m_, p_):8.4f}  "
              f"1/S={1/certified_value(m_, p_):.6f}  slack={slack:+.6f}  "
              f"feasible={slack >= -1e-15}")
    print("  -> the verdict never flips: it is insensitive to the precision of P-hat.")
    print()
    print("  Superseded / stale readings:")
    for label, val in (("drafted 5.19 window", 5.1948), ("certified anchor", 5.4054)):
        print(f"    {label:22s}: {val}")
    print(f"    stale locus (0.115, 0.87): S = {certified_value(0.115, 0.87):.4f}")
    print()


def demo_composition() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("9. Composition: 1/S is a Bernoulli agreement probability")
    print("=" * 78)
    # Monte-Carlo check that D is an agreement probability.
    rng = random.Random(99)
    mu, P = 0.37, 0.71
    n = 400000
    agree = sum(1 for _ in range(n) if (rng.random() < mu) == (rng.random() < P))
    print(f"  D({mu}, {P}) = {agreement(mu, P):.6f}   Monte-Carlo agreement rate = "
          f"{agree/n:.6f}   (n = {n})")
    print()
    print("  Strict submultiplicativity  S(mu1*mu2, P1*P2) < S1 * S2:")
    print("      (mu1,P1)      (mu2,P2)     composite      product      slack")
    for (a, b, c_, d) in ((0.5, 0.9, 0.5, 0.999), (0.2, 0.8, 0.4, 0.7),
                          (0.05, 0.85, 0.1, 0.9), (0.3, 0.6, 0.3, 0.6)):
        comp = certified_value(a * c_, b * d)
        prod = certified_value(a, b) * certified_value(c_, d)
        print(f"   ({a:.2f},{b:.3f})  ({c_:.2f},{d:.3f})  {comp:10.6f}  {prod:10.6f}  "
              f"{prod - comp:+.6f}")
    print("  boundary case (mu1,P1)=(1/2,9/10), (mu2,P2)=(1/2,1): "
          f"composite = {certified_value(0.25, 0.9):.6f}, product = "
          f"{certified_value(0.5, 0.9) * certified_value(0.5, 1.0):.6f}")
    print("  -> reporting a composed guarantee as a product is conservative, never")
    print("     optimistic.")
    print()


def demo_canonical_prior() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("10. The canonical reporting prior b(r) = 0.5 r^{-3/2}")
    print("=" * 78)
    for R in (1.5, 2.0, 4.0, 10.0, 100.0):
        num = numeric_integral(canonical_kernel, 1.0, R, 20000)

demos.name: Exact Anchor-Table Re-Derivation and Erratum Detector
demos.description: Recomputes every entry of a positional-stratum anchor table in exact rational arithmetic from the stored measurement, so the audit itself introduces no rounding. For each anchor it prints the certified value at the stored P̂, the value at P̂ rounded to three decimals, the printed value, the discrepancy, the descending-baseline value, and the feasibility slack (1−P)(1−2μ). Running it isolates the erratum: the row (0.02, 0.9853) prints 29.0698, which is exactly the law at the rounded input 0.985, whereas the stored measurement gives 15625/533 = 29.3152; it also confirms that every feasibility verdict is unaffected.
demos.code:
"""Exact re-derivation of a positional-stratum anchor table, with erratum detection.

Every entry is recomputed in exact rational arithmetic from the stored measurement, so no
rounding is introduced by the audit itself.  For each anchor the script reports:

  * the certified value S = 1/(mu P + (1-mu)(1-P)) at the STORED measurement;
  * the value at the measurement ROUNDED to three decimals -- the classic source of
    printed-table discrepancies;
  * the value against the descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2, which is smaller by the exact
    factor (M+1)/(2M) and tends to half the certified number;
  * the feasibility slack D - mu = (1-P)(1-2mu), whose nonnegativity on mu <= 1/2 proves
    that no feasibility verdict can be flipped by re-reading the measurement.

Running it reproduces the erratum: the row (0.02, 0.9853) is printed as 29.0698, which is
the law at the rounded input 0.985; at the stored measurement the value is 29.3152.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, NamedTuple


class Anchor(NamedTuple):
    mu: Fraction
    p_stored: Fraction
    printed: float
    note: str


def agreement(mu: Fraction, p: Fraction) -> Fraction:
    return mu * p + (1 - mu) * (1 - p)


def certified_value(mu: Fraction, p: Fraction) -> Fraction:
    return 1 / agreement(mu, p)


def round_to(p: Fraction, decimals: int) -> Fraction:
    scale = Fraction(10) ** decimals
    return Fraction(round(p * scale), scale)


def main() -> None:
    M = 10 ** 6
    anchors: List[Anchor] = [
        Anchor(Fraction(2, 100), Fraction(9853, 10000), 29.0698, "printed at rounded P"),
        Anchor(Fraction(5, 100), Fraction(85, 100), 5.19, "printed from a drafted form"),
        Anchor(Fraction(52, 1000), Fraction(85, 100), 5.3648, "same-prior adversary"),
        Anchor(Fraction(115, 1000), Fraction(87, 100), 4.649, "stale prose locus"),
    ]

    header = (f"{'mu':>7} {'P stored':>10} {'S stored':>10} {'S rounded':>10} "
              f"{'printed':>9} {'shift':>8} {'S vs C0':>9} {'slack':>9} {'feas':>6}  note")
    print(header)
    print("-" * len(header))
    for a in anchors:
        s_stored = certified_value(a.mu, a.p_stored)
        s_round = certified_value(a.mu, round_to(a.p_stored, 3))
        s_desc = s_stored * Fraction(M + 1, 2 * M)
        slack = (1 - a.p_stored) * (1 - 2 * a.mu)
        print(f"{float(a.mu):7.3f} {float(a.p_stored):10.4f} {float(s_stored):10.4f} "
              f"{float(s_round):10.4f} {a.printed:9.4f} "
              f"{float(s_stored) - a.printed:8.4f} {float(s_desc):9.4f} "
              f"{float(slack):9.6f} {str(slack >= 0):>6}  {a.note}")

    print()
    print("Erratum detected:")
    mu, p_stored = Fraction(2, 100), Fraction(9853, 10000)
    s_stored = certified_value(mu, p_stored)
    s_round = certified_value(mu, round_to(p_stored, 3))
    print(f"  row (0.02, 0.9853) prints 29.0698 = S(0.02, 0.985) = {s_round} "
          f"= {float(s_round):.6f}")
    print(f"  correct entry at the stored measurement    = {s_stored} "
          f"= {float(s_stored):.6f}")
    print(f"  shift = {float(s_stored - s_round):.4f}: the fourth decimal of the stored")
    print("  measurement carries a quarter of a unit of value at mu = 0.02.")
    print("  Feasibility of all anchors is unaffected: the slack (1-P)(1-2mu) is")
    print("  nonnegative on the whole admissible half-box mu <= 1/2.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

algorithms.name: Sharp Booked-Envelope Evaluation and Booking-Consistency Audit
algorithms.description: Given only the bookings (M, m, P) — slot count, head-stratum size and capture probability — this procedure returns the exact range of expected scan cost compatible with them, together with the uniform-cells point prediction and a verdict on a measured cost. The mathematical foundation is the envelope theorem: splitting the expectation over the head stratum and its complement and bounding each slot index by the extremes of its block gives P + (1−P)(m+1) ≤ EC ≤ Pm + (1−P)M, and the two-atom head and tail witnesses show both ends are attained, so the interval cannot be narrowed without booking a further statistic. Because the interval is exactly attainable, a measured cost outside it is a certificate that the reported bookings do not describe the workload — an audit test requiring no distributional assumption. Complexity: O(1) for the envelope and the verdict, O(M) if a full weight vector is supplied and its expected cost evaluated.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT   M (slots), m (head stratum size), P (capture probability),
        measured_EC (observed expected cost)
REQUIRE 1 <= m <= M and 0 <= P <= 1

1.  lower  <- P * 1 + (1 - P) * (m + 1)      // all mass as early as possible
2.  upper  <- P * m + (1 - P) * M            // all mass as late as possible
3.  booked <- P * (m + 1)/2 + (1 - P) * (m + (M - m + 1)/2)
4.  width  <- upper - lower                  // = P(m-1) + (1-P)(M-m-1)
5.  inside <- (lower <= measured_EC <= upper)
6.  IF inside THEN verdict <- "bookings consistent"
    ELSE verdict <- "BOOKING VIOLATION: cost outside the sharp envelope"
7.  RETURN (lower, upper, width, booked, inside, verdict)

REMARK  lower is attained by the head witness (mass 1-1/m at slot 1,
        mass 1/m at slot m+1 when M = 2m); upper is attained by the tail
        witness (mass P at slot m, mass 1-P at slot M).  Hence no bound
        stated in terms of (M, m, P) alone can be tighter.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm A: sharp booked-envelope evaluation and admissibility audit."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Sequence, Tuple


def booked_ec(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> float:
    """Uniform-within-cells booked expected scan cost for a head stratum of size m."""
    return P * ((m + 1) / 2.0) + (1.0 - P) * (m + (M - m + 1) / 2.0)


def booked_envelope(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Exact range of the expected scan cost over ALL weights honouring (M, m, P).

    Lower end: all captured mass at slot 1, all escaping mass at slot m+1.
    Upper end: all captured mass at slot m, all escaping mass at slot M.
    """
    if not (1 <= m <= M):
        raise ValueError("require 1 <= m <= M")
    if not (0.0 <= P <= 1.0):
        raise ValueError("require 0 <= P <= 1")
    return P * 1.0 + (1.0 - P) * (m + 1), P * m + (1.0 - P) * M


def expected_scan_cost(weight: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """EC = sum_i i * w(i) with slots numbered 1..M."""
    return sum((i + 1) * w for i, w in enumerate(weight))


def audit_bookings(M: int, m: int, P: float, measured_ec: float) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Audit a measured expected cost against the bookings (M, m, P).

    Returns the envelope, the booked point prediction, the booking factor implied
    by the measurement on the head stratum, and a verdict.  A measured cost outside
    the envelope certifies that the reported bookings do not describe the workload.
    """
    lo, hi = booked_envelope(M, m, P)
    booked = booked_ec(M, m, P)
    centre_head = (m + 1) / 2.0
    return {
        "envelope_lower": lo,
        "envelope_upper": hi,
        "envelope_width": hi - lo,
        "booked_prediction": booked,
        "measured": measured_ec,
        "inside_envelope": lo - 1e-12 <= measured_ec <= hi + 1e-12,
        "booked_relative_error": (booked - measured_ec) / measured_ec,
        "head_cell_centre": centre_head,
        "verdict": (
            "bookings consistent" if lo - 1e-12 <= measured_ec <= hi + 1e-12
            else "BOOKING VIOLATION: measured cost outside the sharp envelope"
        ),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Head witness on M = 2m attains the lower end exactly.
    m = 16
    M = 2 * m
    P = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
    w = [0.0] * M
    w[0], w[m] = 1.0 - 1.0 / m, 1.0 / m
    report = audit_bookings(M, m, P, expected_scan_cost(w))
    for key, value in report.items():
        print(f"{key:24s}: {value}")

algorithms.name: Certified-Value Audit with Baseline Correction and Rounding Sensitivity
algorithms.description: A one-locus audit of a reported speedup. It evaluates the certified value S = 1/D with D = μP + (1−μ)(1−P) in exact rational arithmetic at the stored measurement, repeats the evaluation at the measurement rounded to a chosen precision, converts to the descending baseline via the exact factor (M+1)/(2M), and reports the feasibility slack D − μ = (1−P)(1−2μ). The three outputs correspond to the three ways a value claim leaks: an unnamed baseline (worth a factor tending to two), an unpinned locus, and a rounded input. The feasibility slack is an exact factorisation, nonnegative precisely on the admissible half-box μ ≤ 1/2, which is why a rounding correction can move a printed value without moving any feasibility verdict. All arithmetic is over the rationals, so the audit introduces no error of its own. Complexity: O(1).
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT   mu, P_stored (exact rationals), M (slot count), decimals d

1.  D_stored  <- mu*P_stored + (1-mu)*(1-P_stored)
2.  S_stored  <- 1 / D_stored
3.  P_round   <- round(P_stored * 10^d) / 10^d
4.  S_round   <- 1 / (mu*P_round + (1-mu)*(1-P_round))
5.  factor    <- (M + 1) / (2M)              // in (1/2, 1) for M > 1
6.  S_desc    <- S_stored * factor           // value vs the descending baseline
7.  slack     <- (1 - P_stored) * (1 - 2*mu) // equals D - mu, exactly
8.  feasible  <- (slack >= 0)                // always true when mu <= 1/2
9.  RETURN (S_stored, S_round, S_stored - S_round, S_desc, factor,
            slack, feasible)

REMARK  Step 3 reproduces the classic table error: printing S at a rounded
        input.  At mu = 0.02 the law is steep in P, so d = 3 already shifts
        the value by about a quarter of a unit.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm B: certified-value audit with baseline correction and rounding sensitivity."""

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Dict, Union

Number = Union[float, Fraction]


def agreement(mu: Number, P: Number) -> Number:
    """D(mu, P) = mu P + (1-mu)(1-P): the Bernoulli agreement probability, equal to 1/S."""
    return mu * P + (1 - mu) * (1 - P)


def certified_value(mu: Number, P: Number) -> Number:
    """S(mu, P) = 1 / D(mu, P), stated against the full-scan-M baseline."""
    return 1 / agreement(mu, P)


def descending_value(M: Number, mu: Number, P: Number) -> Number:
    """Value of the same algorithm against the descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2."""
    return certified_value(mu, P) * (M + 1) / (2 * M)


def feasibility_slack(mu: Number, P: Number) -> Number:
    """D - mu = (1-P)(1-2mu): nonnegative exactly on the admissible half-box mu <= 1/2."""
    return (1 - P) * (1 - 2 * mu)


def audit_locus(mu: Fraction, P_stored: Fraction, M: int, decimals: int = 3) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Full audit of one anchor of a value table.

    Reports the exact certified value at the stored measurement, the value at the
    rounded measurement (the classic source of printed-table errors), the
    descending-baseline correction, and the feasibility verdict.  All arithmetic is
    exact rational arithmetic, so no rounding is introduced by the audit itself.
    Cost: O(1).
    """
    scale = Fraction(10) ** decimals
    P_round = Fraction(round(P_stored * scale), scale)
    S_stored = certified_value(mu, P_stored)
    S_round = certified_value(mu, P_round)
    return {
        "mu": float(mu),
        "P_stored": float(P_stored),
        "P_rounded": float(P_round),
        "S_stored_exact": S_stored,
        "S_stored": float(S_stored),
        "S_rounded": float(S_round),
        "rounding_shift": float(S_stored - S_round),
        "S_descending_baseline": float(descending_value(M, mu, P_stored)),
        "baseline_factor": float(Fraction(M + 1, 2 * M)),
        "feasibility_slack": float(feasibility_slack(mu, P_stored)),
        "feasible": feasibility_slack(mu, P_stored) >= 0,
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    report = audit_locus(Fraction(2, 100), Fraction(9853, 10000), M=10 ** 6)
    for key, value in report.items():
        print(f"{key:24s}: {value}")

algorithms.name: Adversarial Locus Extremisation by Corner Enumeration
algorithms.description: Finds the best and worst certified value achievable inside an admissible rectangle of loci. The mathematical foundation is bilinearity: D(μ,P) = μP + (1−μ)(1−P) has partial derivatives ∂D/∂μ = 2P − 1 and ∂D/∂P = 2μ − 1, each of constant sign on a half-box, so D is monotone in each coordinate separately and attains its extrema at the corners of any axis-aligned box; since S = 1/D is a decreasing function of D, so does S. The search therefore needs four evaluations rather than a grid, and the routine includes an optional brute-force confirmation over a dense grid. Applied to the certified anchor (0.05, 0.85) with μ perturbed to 0.052 it returns 5.3648… < 5.4054…, showing that the certified number is not a locus-free guarantee. Complexity: O(1) for the corner search; O(g²) for the optional grid confirmation at resolution g.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT   mu_range = [mu_lo, mu_hi], P_range = [P_lo, P_hi]

1.  corners <- { (mu, P) : mu in {mu_lo, mu_hi}, P in {P_lo, P_hi} }
2.  FOR each (mu, P) in corners:
        D  <- mu*P + (1-mu)*(1-P)
        S  <- 1 / D
3.  (S_min, locus_min) <- argmin over corners
4.  (S_max, locus_max) <- argmax over corners
5.  spread <- S_max - S_min
6.  RETURN (corners with values, S_min, locus_min, S_max, locus_max, spread)

JUSTIFICATION  D is bilinear: dD/dmu = 2P - 1 and dD/dP = 2mu - 1 have
        constant sign on each half-box, so D is monotone in each coordinate
        and its extrema over an axis-aligned box sit at corners.  S = 1/D is
        strictly decreasing in D, so the same corners extremise S.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm C: adversarial locus search over an admissible box (corner enumeration)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


def agreement(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """D(mu, P) = mu P + (1-mu)(1-P)."""
    return mu * P + (1.0 - mu) * (1.0 - P)


def certified_value(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    """S(mu, P) = 1 / D(mu, P)."""
    return 1.0 / agreement(mu, P)


def adversarial_locus(
    mu_range: Tuple[float, float], P_range: Tuple[float, float]
) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Extremise the certified value over an axis-aligned admissible box.

    D is bilinear, with partial derivatives d/dmu D = 2P - 1 and d/dP D = 2mu - 1,
    each of constant sign on a half-box.  Hence D -- and therefore S = 1/D -- attains
    its extrema at the corners of the box, and the search is O(1): four evaluations,
    independent of any grid resolution.
    """
    corners: List[Tuple[float, float]] = list(product(mu_range, P_range))
    values = [(certified_value(m, p), m, p) for m, p in corners]
    worst = min(values)
    best = max(values)
    return {
        "corners": [(m, p, certified_value(m, p)) for m, p in corners],
        "min_value": worst[0],
        "min_locus": (worst[1], worst[2]),
        "max_value": best[0],
        "max_locus": (best[1], best[2]),
        "spread": best[0] - worst[0],
    }


def verify_corner_optimality(
    mu_range: Tuple[float, float], P_range: Tuple[float, float], grid: int = 400
) -> bool:
    """Brute-force confirmation that the extrema really sit at corners."""
    lo_mu, hi_mu = mu_range
    lo_P, hi_P = P_range
    report = adversarial_locus(mu_range, P_range)
    tol = 1e-9
    for i in range(grid + 1):
        for j in range(grid + 1):
            mu = lo_mu + (hi_mu - lo_mu) * i / grid
            P = lo_P + (hi_P - lo_P) * j / grid
            s = certified_value(mu, P)
            if s > float(report["max_value"]) + tol or s < float(report["min_value"]) - tol:
                return False
    return True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # The certified anchor (0.05, 0.85), perturbed within an admissible neighbourhood.
    out = adversarial_locus((0.050, 0.052), (0.85, 0.85))
    print(f"certified anchor S(0.05, 0.85) = {certified_value(0.05, 0.85):.6f}")
    print(f"adversarial minimum over the box = {out['min_value']:.6f} at {out['min_locus']}")
    print(f"corner optimality verified: {verify_corner_optimality((0.04, 0.06), (0.80, 0.90))}")

visualizations.name: The Sharp Envelope and the Unbounded Divergence of the Booked Law
visualizations.description: Two panels. The left shades the exact range of expected scan cost compatible with the bookings as the head-stratum size m grows (with M = 2m and P = 1 − 1/m), overlays the two extremal witnesses that attain the ends, and traces the uniform-cells booked prediction through the interior. The right plots the ratio of the booked prediction to the true cost of the head witness, which equals (m+3)/4 and diverges — the geometric statement of the failure of value-universality.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: the sharp booked envelope versus the booked point law.

Plots, as a function of the head-stratum size m inside M = 2m slots, the exact range of
expected scan cost compatible with the bookings (shaded), the booked (uniform-cells)
point prediction, and the two extremal witnesses.  The divergence between the head
witness and the booked curve is the unbounded failure of value-universality.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def booked_ec(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> float:
    return P * ((m + 1) / 2.0) + (1.0 - P) * (m + (M - m + 1) / 2.0)


def envelope(M: int, m: int, P: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    return P * 1.0 + (1.0 - P) * (m + 1), P * m + (1.0 - P) * M


def main() -> None:
    ms: List[int] = list(range(2, 65))
    lo: List[float] = []
    hi: List[float] = []
    booked: List[float] = []
    for m in ms:
        M = 2 * m
        P = 1.0 - 1.0 / m
        a, b = envelope(M, m, P)
        lo.append(a)
        hi.append(b)
        booked.append(booked_ec(M, m, P))

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))

    ax = axes[0]
    ax.fill_between(ms, lo, hi, alpha=0.25, color="#3b7dd8",
                    label="admissible range (sharp envelope)")
    ax.plot(ms, lo, color="#1b4f9c", lw=2, label="head witness (lower end, $EC=2$)")
    ax.plot(ms, hi, color="#1b4f9c", lw=2, ls="--", label="tail witness (upper end)")
    ax.plot(ms, booked, color="#d1495b", lw=2.5,
            label="booked uniform-cells prediction")
    ax.set_xlabel("head stratum size $m$   (slots $M = 2m$, capture $P = 1 - 1/m$)")
    ax.set_ylabel("expected scan cost")
    ax.set_title("Every booked law lives inside a sharp envelope")
    ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    ax = axes[1]
    ratio = [b / l for b, l in zip(booked, lo)]
    ax.plot(ms, ratio, color="#d1495b", lw=2.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("head stratum size $m$")
    ax.set_ylabel("booked prediction / true cost")
    ax.set_title("Failure of value-universality is unbounded")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.annotate("ratio $=(m+3)/4 \\rightarrow \\infty$", xy=(45, ratio[43]),
                xytext=(15, ratio[-1] * 0.8),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#333333"), fontsize=10)

    fig.suptitle("Positional strata: the booked value law is a report, not a guarantee",
                 fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("envelope_vs_booked.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote envelope_vs_booked.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: The Certified Value Surface and its Feasibility Region
visualizations.description: The left panel maps log₁₀ S(μ,P) over the unit box with the recorded anchors marked — the corrected 29.32 row, the certified 5.41 anchor, the adversarial 5.36 locus and the stale 4.65 locus — and the two symmetry axes S(μ,P) = S(P,μ) and S(μ,P) = S(1−μ,1−P) drawn in. The right panel maps the feasibility slack D − μ = (1−P)(1−2μ), showing it nonnegative on the entire admissible half-box μ ≤ 1/2, which is why re-reading a measurement can move a printed value but never a feasibility verdict.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: the certified value surface, its feasibility region, and the anchors.

Left panel: the surface S(mu, P) = 1/(mu P + (1-mu)(1-P)) on the unit box, with the
recorded anchors marked, the symmetry axes S(mu,P) = S(P,mu) and S(mu,P) = S(1-mu,1-P)
indicated, and the degenerate ridge along the corners.  Right panel: the feasibility
slack D - mu = (1-P)(1-2mu), which is nonnegative on the whole admissible half-box
mu <= 1/2 -- the reason the anchor-table erratum leaves every feasibility verdict intact.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def main() -> None:
    n = 400
    mu = np.linspace(0.005, 0.995, n)
    P = np.linspace(0.005, 0.995, n)
    MU, PP = np.meshgrid(mu, P)
    D = MU * PP + (1 - MU) * (1 - PP)
    S = 1.0 / D
    slack = (1 - PP) * (1 - 2 * MU)

    anchors = [(0.02, 0.9853, "corrected 29.32", (8, -4)),
               (0.05, 0.85, "certified 5.41", (10, -14)),
               (0.052, 0.85, "adversary 5.36", (10, -26)),
               (0.115, 0.87, "stale 4.65", (10, 6))]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13.5, 5.4))

    ax = axes[0]
    im = ax.pcolormesh(MU, PP, np.log10(S), shading="auto", cmap="magma")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label=r"$\log_{10} S(\mu, P)$")
    ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color="white", lw=1, ls=":", alpha=0.8)
    ax.plot([0, 1], [1, 0], color="white", lw=1, ls=":", alpha=0.8)
    for m_, p_, label, off in anchors:
        ax.plot(m_, p_, "o", color="#7CFC00", ms=6)
        ax.annotate(label, (m_, p_), textcoords="offset points", xytext=off,
                    color="white", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel(r"retained fraction $\mu$")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"capture probability $P$")
    ax.set_title(r"Certified value $S = 1/\left(\mu P + (1-\mu)(1-P)\right)$")

    ax = axes[1]
    im = ax.pcolormesh(MU, PP, slack, shading="auto", cmap="coolwarm",
                       vmin=-1, vmax=1)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label=r"feasibility slack $D - \mu = (1-P)(1-2\mu)$")
    ax.axvline(0.5, color="black", lw=1.5, ls="--")
    ax.annotate(r"$\mu = 1/2$: boundary of the admissible half-box",
                xy=(0.5, 0.08), xytext=(0.08, 0.08), fontsize=9,
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="black"))
    for m_, p_, _, _off in anchors:
        ax.plot(m_, p_, "o", color="black", ms=5)
    ax.set_xlabel(r"retained fraction $\mu$")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"capture probability $P$")
    ax.set_title(r"Feasibility $\mu \leq 1/S$ holds on all of $\mu \leq 1/2$")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("value_surface.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote value_surface.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: Baseline Conditionality and the Coupling Slack of Composition
visualizations.description: The left panel shows the same algorithm valued against two baselines as a function of the slot count: constant against the full-scan baseline, and S(M+1)/(2M) against the descending baseline, sliding down to exactly half as M grows. The right panel contrasts the composite value S(μ₁μ₂, P₁P₂) with the product S₁S₂ of the factor values, shading the always-positive coupling slack between them — the reason composed guarantees may be reported as products conservatively but never exactly.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: baseline conditionality and the composition slack.

Left: the same algorithm valued against two baselines.  Against the full-scan-M baseline
its value is S; against the descending baseline C0 = (M+1)/2 it is S(M+1)/(2M), which is
bracketed strictly between S/2 and S and tends to exactly half of S.

Right: composition.  Stacking two independent stratifications multiplies the bookings but
not the values: the composite value S(mu1 mu2, P1 P2) lies strictly below the product
S1 S2, by the coupling slack.  Reporting a composed guarantee as a product is therefore
conservative.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def certified_value(mu: float, P: float) -> float:
    return 1.0 / (mu * P + (1.0 - mu) * (1.0 - P))


def main() -> None:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13.5, 5.2))

    ax = axes[0]
    Ms = np.logspace(0.3, 6, 300)
    S = certified_value(0.05, 0.85)
    ax.axhline(S, color="#1b4f9c", lw=2.5, label=r"$S$ vs full-scan-$M$ baseline")
    ax.axhline(S / 2, color="#888888", lw=1.5, ls=":", label=r"$S/2$ (asymptote)")
    ax.semilogx(Ms, S * (Ms + 1) / (2 * Ms), color="#d1495b", lw=2.5,
                label=r"$S\,(M+1)/(2M)$ vs descending baseline $C_0$")
    ax.set_xlabel("slot count $M$")
    ax.set_ylabel("value of the same algorithm")
    ax.set_title(r"Baseline conditionality at the anchor $(\mu,P)=(0.05,0.85)$")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    ax = axes[1]
    ps = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 200)
    comp = [certified_value(0.5 * 0.5, p * 0.9) for p in ps]
    prod = [certified_value(0.5, p) * certified_value(0.5, 0.9) for p in ps]
    ax.plot(ps, prod, color="#1b4f9c", lw=2.5, label=r"product $S_1 S_2$ (reported)")
    ax.plot(ps, comp, color="#d1495b", lw=2.5, label=r"composite $S(\mu_1\mu_2, P_1P_2)$")
    ax.fill_between(ps, comp, prod, color="#d1495b", alpha=0.15,
                    label="coupling slack (always positive)")
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$P_1$   (with $\mu_1 = \mu_2 = 1/2$, $P_2 = 0.9$)")
    ax.set_ylabel("value")
    ax.set_title("Composition is strictly submultiplicative")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("baseline_and_composition.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote baseline_and_composition.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_demos.html:
The Positional-Stratum Value Laboratory

A retrieval algorithm commits to a block of relative size μ before probing, and captures the target inside that block with probability P. Its expected cost is M·D with the agreement probability D = μP + (1−μ)(1−P), and its value is 1/D — but only against a named baseline and at a pinned locus. Move the sliders and watch the value, the baseline correction, the feasibility slack, and the sharp cost envelope respond.

rounding shift

The two symmetries are visible in the heat map: S(μ,P) = S(P,μ) — balance is position — and S(μ,P) = S(1−μ,1−P). The bright corners are the degenerate loci where the two coins almost always disagree.

Value surface and your locus

Brightness is log₁₀ S. The white cross marks your locus; the amber cross marks the certified anchor (0.05, 0.85), whose value is 200/37 = 5.4054…. Drag μ two parts in a thousand to the right and you land strictly below it: the certified number is not a locus-free guarantee.

interactive_demos.title: The r̄-Identity Workbench
interactive_demos.description: A hands-on laboratory for the universal object. Eight vertical sliders shape the weight on the ranked slots and a boundary slider chooses where the retained stratum ends; the panel then reports the capture mass, both conditional mean costs, both cell centres, both booking factors, the expected cost computed directly, the same quantity computed from the identity, and the residual between them — which stays at machine precision for every shape you can draw. It also reports the uniform-cells prediction and its ratio to the truth, and checks the majorization bound EC ≤ (M+1)/2 whenever the weight you drew is descending. Presets include a flat weight, a head-loaded adversarial weight, and a deliberately non-uniform cell whose booking factor is exactly 1 — the configuration that shows why a single booking factor certifies nothing.
